svg.title: Figure 9-1. Attack paths of the risk-5 threat scenarios (WP-C-09 §5, §9)
svg.desc: For the five risk-5 threat scenarios of §9, the figure traces entry point, attack path, asset reached and the damage scenarios each can cause. Code execution on the SoC (AS-05) is the entry point of AP-02 (to AS-02, TS-02), AP-03 (to AS-03 and AS-04, TS-03), AP-14 (to AS-01 and AS-15, TS-14) and AP-04 (to AS-06 and AS-07, TS-04); AP-08 (TS-08, risk 4) is drawn as the foothold that §5 states yields root on the SoC. Physical possession of the device is the entry point of AP-11 (to AS-11, AS-12, AS-13, TS-11). TS-02 and TS-03 lead to DS-01 to DS-07, TS-14 to DS-01, DS-03, DS-04 and DS-07, TS-04 to DS-01 to DS-06, and TS-11 to DS-08, DS-09, DS-10 and DS-12. All five have feasibility High and impact 4. Treatments for TS-02 and TS-14 are implemented in the reference build only and not verified.
svg.text: Figure 9-1 · Attack paths of the risk-5 threat scenarios
Entry point → attack path summary → asset → damage scenarios, for ranks 1–5 of §9 · abstraction level of §5, no procedural detail
Host → panda command sets a permissive
safety mode or parameter; no authentication
mode lock implemented (reference build), not verified
SoC reprograms the panda MCU through its boot
Host CAN transmit through the panda carries frames
or rates it should refuse (details: GD-11)
TSR-705, TSR-518 in reference build, not verified on HW
Write safety-relevant params or publish forged msgq
Read persisted video, location logs and the identity
Shown: ranks 1–5 of §9 (all impact 4, feasibility High, risk 5). AP-08 is the one foothold that §5 states leads to root on the SoC; the risk-4 and risk-3 paths are listed in §5 and not drawn.
Damage dots follow the “Damage” column of §4; the impact row is the maximum level of §3. Amber: treatment status of 2026-10-12; ratings are of the shipped baseline 8b8c6ae, not re-rated (OI-5).
